pairs.subject: candidate-consent-and-retention
pairs.evidence: app/_lib/consent.ts:38 Consent lifecycle states omit withdrawal and fail open when expiry is missing, while the legal-claims carve-out holds decision records indefinitely without an end date.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/consent.ts:28 Candidate-facing retention months are derived from enforced TTL days and rounded up via Math.ceil so disclosure never understates the window.
app/_lib/consent.ts:68 Treats missing expiry as active rather than withholding, and ConsentStatus lacks a withdrawn state.
app/_lib/erasure-full-scrub.test.ts:257 Regression test asserts that every workspace-scoped table is reached by the single-transaction erasure or listed in ERASURE_EXEMPT.
app/_lib/consent.ts:220 Recursively traverses container subtrees to blank strings and empty arrays while preserving structural shape and scores.
app/_lib/consent.ts:148 Masks candidate labels to initials with stopword stripping so pipeline history remains legible without identifying candidates.
app/_lib/erasure-full-scrub.test.ts:277 Retained carve-out tables require a written reason but carry no limitation period or end date, leaving retention indefinite.

pairs.registryProposal: Clarify in the standard whether consent withdrawal belongs under read-time-gate-not-just-the-sweep or warrants its own named technique, as the golden path mandates append-only withdrawal transitions distinct from expiry.
